name: Amaziah
overview: Amaziah was a male king from the tribe of Judah, known as the son of Joash. He is recognized for doing what was right in the sight of the LORD, though his devotion was not wholehearted. His reign reflects a complex relationship with God, marked by partial obedience and spiritual compromise.
namesAndTitles: The name Amaziah means 'YHWH is powerful,' highlighting a connection to God's strength. His title as King of Judah identifies his royal role over the southern kingdom. These names emphasize both his divine association and political authority.
familyAndRelationships: Amaziah was the son of Joash and the father of Jehoaddin, establishing a direct royal lineage. Additionally, Azariah is noted as his father, which may reflect a generational title or alternate name. Scripture provides these key familial connections, situating Amaziah within the Davidic line.
scriptureSignificance: Amaziah's significance lies in his example of incomplete faithfulness to God. Though he executed justice by punishing his father's murderers according to God's law, his failure to fully trust the LORD led to spiritual and military setbacks. His actions, including adopting foreign gods after victory, demonstrate the dangers of pride and partial obedience, serving as a cautionary figure in the biblical narrative.
